Readable props that quote people: an in-world article or report where the author narrates and an interviewee is quoted. Splitting these gives the quoted speech its own voice instead of the author impersonating everyone. Applied by build_line_segments.py, which cuts the line at each listed quote and emits alternating segments (author, quote, author, ...) exactly as it does for {{GM}} narration - so the keys are the ordinary ~c0/~c1 ones the lab, the dedup and the pack builder already handle, and the pack stitches them back into one continuous read.

The quotes are listed BY HAND on purpose. Splitting on quotation marks automatically gets it wrong in every direction: Street Magic Quarterly quotes the TERM "background count" and the phrase "Deep shit" (not speech at all), and in node 20 the author's own interjections "Laughing?" and "Like, hyena-laughing?" sit inside the interviewee's answer. A rule that could tell those apart reliably does not exist; a list does.

Each entry: the exact quoted substring (verbatim, including its trailing comma) and the voice that says it. Anything not listed stays with the prop's own casting.

dragonfall.prop: Street Magic Quarterly // a Shadowfront Publication
dragonfall.author: Dr. Elizabeth Alder — signed at the end of both articles, called 'Liz' by Hansen and 'Dr. Alder' by Okinyi

9: "You need to get the word out about this, Liz,"
"I'll back you. The community needs to know."

20: "When it was alive, it killed six men - ripped the faces and genitals off of two, and bathed the other four in some sort of caustic fluid. And all the while, it was laughing."
"No. It was laughing like a man."
21: "This was not a simple animal, Dr. Alder. It acted with *purpose* when it killed those men, and the only surviving witness tells me that it grew fat on their screams."
23: "The emergence of magic some forty years ago put a new wrinkle into biological field work,"

"New species are being discovered all the time. But this... this is something different. "These creatures that have been popping up recently fall outside of any meaningful system of classification. And what's more, I have conducted enough autopsies on them to know that they do not belong here."
24: "What I mean to tell you is that their internal anatomy is all wrong. It doesn't even make sense,"
"These creatures could not exist were it not for magic. And six months ago, I would have told you that they could not exist at all."

dragonfall.not_split: Node 4's "background count" and node 7's "Deep shit" are quoted terms, not speech. Node 10's "In trouble," is Alder quoting Hansen back to herself in her closing line. Node 20's "Laughing?" and "Like, hyena-laughing?" are Alder's own questions inside the exchange, and stay hers.

3: "She swooped down on us, crashing through buildings and vomiting flames. I thought that I was sure to die, but a strange-looking elf used his magic to save me."
4: "He shielded me from harm, and then he was consumed by the flames. His companion, a pale elvish woman, went mad... I don't remember anything after that."

6: "Conventional weapons technology is more than capable of bringing down a dragon these days - even one as fearsome as the Firewing. "

10: "The disaster conditions that still plague the city months after Feuerschwinge's second rampage might have contributed to the rapid spread of CSMDS,"

"Much of the city still lacks basic sanitation services, and clean water is difficult to come by. Disaster areas such as Berlin have repeatedly shown themselves to be ideal breeding grounds for disease."

3: "It looks to me like they're hunkering down,"
"preparing themselves for a defensive war. This is unusual for a couple of reasons. "
4: "Short of a global conflict, I can't see what could threaten both Tír na nÓg *and* Tir Tairngire,"
"Maybe the Council of Princes knows something that the rest of us don't. But whatever they're thinking, it's making a lot of people nervous."

13: "The dragons weren't so lucky. We're close to finding a cure, but I'm not sure that we're close enough to save them."
14: "In a way, this is good for us,"

"It is, of course, tragic that so many dragons are dying so horribly of this disease. But this is the first opportunity we've had to watch a slate-wiper virus at work against an intelligent population. "

15: "This disease - or a mutant strain of it - could still do to us what it's doing to the dragons. That's why it's imperative that we find a cure quickly. "
16: "I can't give you a definite time line, but I can say that we'll be ready to move into human trials soon."

18: "Hestaby was one of the most magnificent creatures ever to have lived,"
"It is fitting that the Great Dragons of the world should be memorialized in her image."
